title: Place n Queens So None Attacks Another

concept.title: One queen per row, and a check before every placement
body: A queen attacks along its row, its column and both diagonals. On an `n` by `n` board, `n` queens that do not attack each other must be in **different rows**, so we place exactly one queen in each row, from the top row to the bottom row. The only question in each row is the **column**.

A column is allowed only if no queen above it uses the same column or one of its two diagonals. Cells on the same "\" diagonal have the same value of `row - col`, and cells on the same "/" diagonal have the same value of `row + col`. Three arrays of booleans remember what is taken:

Checking each queen against the earlier ones **before** placing it cuts away the huge part of the search where two queens already attack each other. For `n = 8` there are 92 solutions; the search visits only a few thousand placements instead of billions.

statement: Count the ways to place `n` queens on an `n` by `n` chessboard so that no two queens attack each other (no two in the same row, column or diagonal).

examples.note: There are two placements: queens in columns 2 4 1 3 and 3 1 4 2 of rows 1 to 4.

hints: Put exactly one queen in each row and choose its column.
A column is free if no earlier queen shares the column, the row + col diagonal or the row - col diagonal.
Mark the three things when you place a queen and unmark them when you take it away.

explanation: Each call fills one row. A column is used only when the column and both diagonals are free; they are marked before the recursive call and cleared after it. Reaching the row `n` means all queens are placed.
solution.complexity: Time exponential, about 166 000 placements for n = 11; space O(n).
